subject: services/asr-eval-runtime/medzen_asr_eval/metrics.py normalize_text destroyed every combining mark that cannot precompose, and split the word where it stood. This record states the fix, the tone policy now required of every caller, which published evaluations are affected, and by how much. It corrects two claims and restates NO historical figure.

the_change.after: normalize_text(value, *, policy) — the policy is keyword-only and REQUIRED. A silent default is what made the canonical WER and CER tone-blind with no report saying so.
the_change.before: normalize_text(value) mapped every character that is not alphanumeric, whitespace or an apostrophe to a SPACE. A category-Mn mark surviving NFC is not alphanumeric, so it became a space: the word SPLIT and the mark was DESTROYED. Precomposed vowels are single alphanumeric codepoints and were untouched, so the damage was SELECTIVE — it fell on schwa, open-o, barred-u and open-e, the vowels these orthographies need and Latin-1 lacks.
breaking_by_design: normalize_text() and error_counts() raise TypeError without a named policy.

aggregate() refuses receipts whose rows carry no normalization_policy. Row receipts written before this change carry none, so re-aggregating them fails closed instead of publishing an unlabelled rate.
pilot.py refuses to resume a row receipt scored under a different policy than the current run declares.

declared_defaults.run_pilot: asr-eval-norm-v2-tone-sensitive (overridable, always recorded in the report)
declared_defaults.scripts/build_cameroon_pilot_splits.py: asr-eval-norm-v1-mark-destroying, PINNED. It decides prompt IDENTITY, never a score. v1 is what reproduces the cp1 splits, and it is the conservative choice: destroying marks collapses two prompts differing only in tone into ONE identity, forcing them into the SAME split. It can over-merge prompts; it can never leak one across the train/test boundary.

the_change.labelling: error_counts() stamps normalization_policy into every row's counts, mirroring the per-row normalization_version that pipeline/normalizers.py has carried since B2.4. aggregate() REFUSES rows that declare no policy and REFUSES to pool two policies into one rate, and returns normalization_policy plus a human-readable normalization_policy_label. run_pilot() and scripts/t6_eval_runner.py name their policy and record it in their reports.

policies.asr-eval-norm-v1-mark-destroying: The pre-fix behaviour, byte-for-byte. DEPRECATED. Retained ONLY so an already-published score can be reproduced and shown to be wrong, and so scripts/build_cameroon_pilot_splits.py can keep reproducing the cp1 split partition.
policies.asr-eval-norm-v2-tone-insensitive: Marks removed CONSISTENTLY — from precomposed vowels too. A legitimate metric that must be LABELLED as tone-insensitive wherever it is reported. Same tokenisation as tone-sensitive, so the pair differs only in whether tone is scored.
policies.asr-eval-norm-v2-tone-sensitive: Combining marks kept, attached to their base character. Never emitted as a space. The honest reading for any figure published as WER or CER on a tone-marked language.

what_this_record_does_NOT_do: It does not restate any published WER or CER. Every historical figure stands as published, under the normaliser that produced it.
It does not retroactively correct the ASR base-model pilot tables — that is not computable without re-running inference, and this record says so rather than estimating.
It does not choose a tone policy for future gates. It makes the choice explicit, labelled and refusable; the policy for any gated language remains an owner decision.

identifier_superseded_2026-09-04.what_changed: The tone-sensitive identifier in this record, 'asr-eval-norm-v2-tone-sensitive', has been superseded by 'asr-eval-norm-v3-tone-sensitive'.
identifier_superseded_2026-09-04.why: v2 kept combining marks but still measured CHARACTERS over the NFC stream, so its CER was composition-dependent: a tone error cost a 1-of-1 substitution on a precomposing vowel (a-acute, one codepoint) and a 1-of-2 deletion on one that cannot precompose (schwa-acute, two). v3 measures CER over the NFD stream, so the same error costs the same either way. The two CERs are NOT poolable, which is exactly why the identifier had to move rather than the semantics changing under a fixed name.
identifier_superseded_2026-09-04.tone_insensitive_deliberately_unchanged: 'asr-eval-norm-v2-tone-insensitive' keeps its identifier: it strips every mark, so there is nothing for NFD to move and its character counts are byte-identical before and after the fix. Verified on probe strings.
identifier_superseded_2026-09-04.legacy_v1_unchanged: 'asr-eval-norm-v1-mark-destroying' is frozen, as this record already states.
identifier_superseded_2026-09-04.effect_on_the_pilot_figures: Tone-sensitive in-domain pooled CER moves 13.73 -> 12.38 as reference characters rise 49,938 -> 56,655. See CM-PILOT-SCORING-VERDICT-2026-001 error_decomposition_in_domain.figures_recomputed_under_the_shipped_scorer. No conclusion changes.
